instantiated_cells.justification: The statutory definition of “lobbyist” turns on being employed by a principal or receiving “economic consideration, other than reimbursement for actual expenses,” and if duties are not exclusively lobbying, making lobbying communications on at least 5 days within a reporting period; it does not set any dollar compensation threshold.

The criteria for being a “lobbyist” (and thus needing licensure/authorization to lobby) are based on employment/economic consideration and a 5-days-of-communications test, not on the lobbyist spending a specified dollar amount on lobbying.

cell.condition_text: Itemization of payments to each lobbyist is required only if the total lobbying expenditures/obligations to that lobbyist exceed $200 during the reporting period (principal expense statement).

instantiated_cells.justification: The principal’s expense statement must list the name/address of a lobbyist and the total amount paid to that lobbyist only when amounts to that lobbyist exceed $200 in the reporting period.

The statute imposes filing/reporting duties on principals (expense statements) and provides a principal-only verified-statement exemption up to $500/year, but contains no lobbyist-specific dollar de minimis exemption from filing disclosure.
Reporting is done through principal expense statements and lobbyist status is triggered by a 5-days communications test, with no lobbyist-side exemption keyed to a percentage of compensated time.

arguments.justification: Wisconsin defines when an individual becomes a “lobbyist” using a 5-days-per-reporting-period communications standard rather than any percentage-of-time threshold.
